title: November ’26 Product Release: Compare Your Factories’ Renewable Energy Share
summary: Compare renewable electricity and heat share per factory in Carbonfact, see where each figure comes from, and break down your footprint by renewable level.
body_markdown:
Whether you collect factory energy data yourself or draw on data already collected through the[Carbonfact Suppliers Network](https://suppliers.carbonfact.com/) ,


you can now see the renewable share of electricity and heat for each factory in your Carbonfact Factory view.


The Factory view is where Carbonfact holds what you know about each facility in your supply chain: its supplier, its location and the energy bills behind its emissions. With renewable share next to each factory's footprint, you can compare factories side by side and see where supplier engagement will move your numbers most.


The Carbonfact Suppliers Network is Carbonfact's free program for collecting energy data directly from factories. When a factory shares its bills there, that data flows into your Factory view once the factory is linked to your account.


Here’s what’s new:


-


Renewable share per factory


– renewable electricity and renewable heat, as two columns you can filter and sort in your Factory view


-


A source for every number


– see whether each figure comes from your bills, the Carbonfact Suppliers Network or Carbonfact heuristics


-


Supplier energy bills on the factory page


– bills shared through the Carbonfact Suppliers Network, with their origin and energy mix


-


Renewable level in Explorer & Copilot


– break your footprint down by how much renewable energy each factory uses


## See Which Factories Run on Renewable Energy


Supply chain decarbonization happens one factory at a time. A brand sourcing knitwear from 40 factories across Turkey, Portugal and Bangladesh needs to know which sites already run renewable electricity. Your Factories list now shows two new columns for every factory with energy data: renewable electricity share and renewable heat share, both calculated from the factory's energy bills.


Electricity and heat are split because they lead to different supplier conversations. A dye house can produce 60% of its electricity through solar panels and still fire its boilers with coal. Seeing both figures side by side tells you whether the next ask is a renewable electricity contract, or a cleaner source of heat for its boilers.


## Know Where Every Number Comes From


Next to each renewable share, a Data source column shows where the factory's figures come from. Primary data means energy bills your team uploaded. Carbonfact Suppliers Network means the supplier shared the data directly. Heuristics means no bill is on file yet, and the factory's footprint relies on modeled estimates until one arrives.


## See Your Suppliers' Own Energy Bills


When a supplier shares energy data through the Carbonfact Suppliers Network, those bills now appear on a linked factory's page in your account. An Origin column separates supplier-shared bills from the ones your team uploaded, and energy mix bars above the list show how the factory's consumption splits across sources such as solar, wind and grid electricity.


Every supplier that joins the Carbonfact Suppliers Network adds energy data you can see, check and use in your own reporting, without another round of data requests.


## Break Down Your Footprint by Renewable Level


How much of your footprint is made in factories running on 100% renewable electricity? Which factories at 0% carry the most footprint? How do your Tier 1 factories compare with your Tier 2 factories, and which countries hold the most footprint in low-renewable factories? Explorer can now break down factory renewable energy, so you can answer these questions and more – or just ask Copilot, and it will build those dashboards for you.


It also tracks the share of your footprint made in high-renewable factories year over year. Each factory’s renewable level is one figure across all years, so that trend reflects production moving between factories.


## Why This Matters


Supplier engagement programs work when brands can point to specific factories and specific numbers. An aggregate footprint tells you that your supply chain emits. Renewable share per factory tells you where to focus: which sites to prioritize for renewable electricity, which need a plan for process heat, and which you still hold no data for. With every figure traced back to a bill and its origin, those supplier conversations, and the climate reports that follow them, rest on numbers you can defend.


Reach out to us onsuppliers@carbonfact.com if you want to join our free data collection program – more than 25 brands already participate. You only need to introduce us to your factory contacts, and we’ll collect the data together with the factory for you.
